orig: Customers choosing to upgrade obtain a license key from Kasten, or install from cloud marketplaces [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.3].
prop: Customers choosing to upgrade obtain a license key, or install from cloud marketplaces [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.3].
why: Legacy-brand drift. glossary.md bans "Kasten by Veeam" and "Kasten K10" as retired phrasing; bare "Kasten" used as the vendor name is the same problem in shorter form — the vendor is Veeam and the product is Veeam Kasten for Kubernetes. Dropping the vendor rather than substituting "Veeam" keeps the sentence inside what p.3 supports (prefer omission over assertion). The same page has a second instance two rows down — "The documentation points at the Kasten product page for a comparison of the editions rather than listing one" (l.483) → "The documentation points at the product page for a comparison of the editions rather than listing one" — apply both. These are the only two bare-vendor "Kasten" uses in the six files; everything else is correctly "Veeam Kasten" or a verbatim string.

orig: Starter — also called Veeam Kasten Free
prop: Veeam Kasten Free — the Starter edition
why: Cross-lesson terminology. Lesson01 leads with "Starter" and treats "Veeam Kasten Free" as an alias; Lesson03 Section 1 leads with the opposite — "Veeam Kasten is available in two main editions, Veeam Kasten Free and Enterprise" and "Veeam Kasten Free is the default Starter edition". A learner meeting the editions in Module 01 and again in Module 03 sees the primary name swap. Put the product-branded name first in both places and keep "Starter" as the descriptor, which also matches how the edition is licensed and sold. Lesson01's body text and the following "Heads up" note reference "the Starter edition" three times (l.462, l.479, l.493) — those read correctly once the heading establishes the pairing, so no further edits are needed. Rubric 5, internally consistent terminology.

orig: You select a Veeam Repository as the Export Location Profile on a new policy. What happens to how volume snapshots are exported?
prop: { "q": "Your team wants to prove Veeam Kasten works on a small test cluster before buying anything, then move the same configuration into production. What does the edition difference mean for that plan?", "opts": [ { "t": "The proof of concept has to be rebuilt for production, because the Enterprise edition uses different container images and a different install process.", "correct": false, "why": "The opposite: both editions use the same container images and follow an identical install process, so the install you rehearse is the install you run [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.3]." }, { "t": "The test cluster can run the free Starter edition, which is functionally the same as Enterprise — but it is limited on support and scale, so production needs the licensed edition.", "correct": true, "why": "Correct on both halves. Starter is the default edition, provided at no charge and intended for evaluation or small non-production clusters, and is functionally the same as Enterprise but limited from a support and scale perspective [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.2]. Same images, same install process [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.3] — what changes is what you are entitled to when a restore matters." }, { "t": "Nothing changes at all: the editions are identical, so the Starter edition is a supported production deployment.", "correct": false, "why": "\u2018Functionally the same\u2019 is not \u2018the same\u2019. The limits are on support and scale, and those are exactly what you need on a bad day [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.2]." } ] }
why: Rubric 2, objective-to-assessment alignment. Module 01 states five objectives; objective 4 ("Describe what Veeam Kasten puts inside a cluster, and how its two editions differ") is the only one with no question against it, while objectives 5 gets two (Q4 and Q5 are both Veeam Backup & Replication export items). Worse, at course level Q4 is a near-duplicate of Lesson03's knowledge-check Q5 — same stem premise (selecting a Veeam Repository as the Export Location Profile), same correct answer (block mode export is enabled automatically), same source pages. Retargeting this one item onto the editions closes the objective gap and removes the duplicate in a single change; Q5 already covers the Veeam Backup & Replication integration for objective 5, and the block-mode rule stays taught in Section 05's constraints table. Apply by replacing the whole question object whose stem is the orig text with the object in prop (the stem is quoted as orig only to pin the location unambiguously).

loc: Lesson02_Kubernetes_Foundations_for_Backup_Admins.html · hero (addition — after the hero__meta block, matching Lesson01/Lesson03)
prop: Before you start: Module 01 — the Veeam Data Platform to Veeam Kasten concept map, and the snapshot-versus-export distinction this module builds on. No Kubernetes knowledge is assumed: every term used here is either defined on the spot or named as coming later.
why: Course-level pattern break. Lesson01 and Lesson03 both open with a prereqs panel — Lesson03's is explicit that Modules 01 and 02 supply "the Kubernetes terms used here without re-definition" — and index.html tells the learner "Module 02 builds on the concept map from Module 01". Module 02 is the one module that states no entry condition, yet it is the hinge the whole course leans on: Module 03 is unrunnable without it. Its hero blurb points forward ("the mental model you will install against") but never backward. Adding the panel makes the chain visible at the point of entry rather than only on the landing page. Modules 04 and 05 state the chain in their hero blurbs ("Modules 01 to 03 got you…", "The four modules before this one built the platform"), so they need no panel — this is the only real gap. Rubric 2 and Rubric 5.

orig: the deployment and release information available from Helm v3, and all of the persistent storage resources associated with those workloads, meaning the PersistentVolumeClaims and PersistentVolumes [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.346].
prop: the deployment and release information available from Helm v3 — Helm is Kubernetes' package manager, covered fully in Module 02, so file the term away rather than chasing it now — and all of the persistent storage resources associated with those workloads, meaning the PersistentVolumeClaims and PersistentVolumes [Src: Kasten Docs 9.0.2 p.346].
why: This is the very first substantive paragraph of the very first lesson, aimed at an audience with zero Kubernetes exposure, and it drops 'Helm v3' as a bare proper noun with no gloss and no signal that it will be explained later. In a live read-aloud this is exactly where a backup admin interrupts with 'wait, what's Helm?' and the presenter has nothing to say except 'hang on, Module 02.' The course already handles this well elsewhere (the hero prereqs box promises every term is 'defined on the spot or deferred to Module 02') — this is the one spot in the opening minutes where that promise isn't kept inline. A four-word parenthetical closes the gap without touching the cited fact.

"VBR" appears nowhere else in the six files — every prose mention is the full "Veeam Backup & Replication", so the abbreviation is never expanded for the learner before the rail tooltip uses it. glossary.md requires "Veeam Backup & Replication (VBR)" on first use before "VBR" is acceptable; the full name will not fit a rail label, so the neutral short form is the fix. The dot's aria-label is already correct ("Jump to the Veeam Backup and Replication repository section"), so only the visible label changes. Same applies to the section comment on l.505 if the LXD wants it tidy.
